tagline: A big Andaman island with white-sand beaches, a Sino-Portuguese old town, and Hokkien food
introHtml:
Phuket is a large island on the Andaman coast that gives you two worlds in one province. The west side is a string of white-sand beaches running from Patong to Kata and Karon down to the quieter Nai Harn, while in Phuket Town there's an old quarter of pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses you can spend a whole day wandering and stopping into cafes.

People come to Phuket to laze on the sand, take boats out to the Phi Phi Islands and Phang Nga Bay, head up to pay respects at the Big Buddha on Nakkerd Hill, and eat local Hokkien dishes like Hokkien mee and oh tao in the old town. It's a coastal province where beaches, islands, and old Chinese culture all mix together.
bestTime: November–April brings clear skies, calm seas, and clear water — perfect for the beach and island boat trips. May–October is monsoon season with heavy rain and rough surf.

highlights.name: Phuket Old Town
highlights.blurb: Thalang Road, Dibuk Road, and Soi Romanee are lined with pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses, full of cafes, old eateries, and souvenir shops. Good for a full day of photos and snacking.

highlights.name: Patong Beach
highlights.blurb: The island's busiest beach and main tourist area, with hotels, restaurants, and Bangla Road buzzing at night. This is where the most foreign visitors gather.

highlights.name: Kata–Karon Beach
highlights.blurb: Two long white-sand beaches south of Patong, more relaxed, with clear water that's good for swimming and surfing when the swell picks up. The Karon Viewpoint is nearby for a photo stop.

highlights.name: Phuket Big Buddha
highlights.blurb: A large white Buddha statue on Nakkerd Hill, visible from many parts of the island. Head up to pay respects and take in sea views over both Chalong Bay and Kata Beach.

highlights.name: Laem Phromthep
highlights.blurb: The cape at the island's southern tip and a popular sunset spot. In the evening, crowds gather across the viewing area to watch the sun drop into the Andaman Sea.

highlights.name: Islands Around Phuket
highlights.blurb: Boats run from the piers to Phi Phi, Coral (Hae) Island, Maiton Island, and Phang Nga Bay on a single-day trip — snorkeling over coral and kayaking among the limestone karsts.

foodScene.name: Phuket Hokkien mee
foodScene.note: Yellow egg noodles, stir-fried or blanched and topped with thick broth, with pork, shrimp, and vegetables. A local Hokkien dish you'll find at the old eateries in the old town.

foodScene.name: Oh tao and local sweets
foodScene.note: Oh tao is oysters fried with batter and taro, crisp outside and soft inside, a popular old-town snack eaten alongside dumplings and morning dim sum.

foodScene.name: Andaman seafood
foodScene.note: Sea on every side means fresh shrimp, shellfish, crab, fish, and lobster. Seafood spots on the beach and in town do it grilled, steamed with lime, stir-fried with curry powder, or in tom yum.

foodScene.name: Bold southern Thai food
foodScene.note: Gaeng tai pla, yellow curry, khua kling, and stir-fried stink beans with shrimp, eaten with hot rice and fresh raw vegetables. A local meal you'll find all over the island.

foodScene.name: Morning dim sum and old-style coffee
foodScene.note: Phuket has an old Chinese community, and dim sum shops open early with steamed buns, har gow, and dumplings, eaten with old-style coffee or hot tea — a local breakfast.

foodScene.name: Roti and pulled tea at Muslim shops
foodScene.note: Roti and pulled-tea shops open from morning until late. The roti is crisp outside and soft inside, eaten with curry or drizzled with milk, washed down with hot pulled tea. Found in town and along the beach.

foodScene.name: Old-town cafes
foodScene.note: Many Sino-Portuguese shophouses have turned into cafes serving fresh coffee with local sweets to linger over — an easy stop for a coffee while wandering the old town.

foodScene.name: Phuket markets and street food
foodScene.note: The Lard Yai walking street on weekends and the town markets have street food, local Hokkien snacks, and grilled seafood to graze on.

attractions.name: Phuket Old Town
attractions.blurb: Thalang Road, Dibuk Road, and Soi Romanee are lined with pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses, full of cafes, old eateries, and souvenir shops to wander and photograph all day.

attractions.name: Patong Beach
attractions.blurb: The island's busiest beach and main tourist area, with hotels, restaurants, and Bangla Road buzzing at night. You can catch boats out to the islands from around here.

attractions.name: Kata and Karon Beach
attractions.blurb: Two long white-sand beaches in the south with clear water and a more relaxed feel than Patong, good for swimming and surfing when the swell is up, with the Karon Viewpoint nearby.

attractions.name: Nakkerd Hill Big Buddha
attractions.blurb: A large white Buddha statue on the hilltop. Head up to pay respects and take in sea views over both Chalong Bay and Kata Beach.

attractions.name: Laem Phromthep
attractions.blurb: The cape at the island's southern tip and a popular sunset spot. In the evening, crowds gather across the viewing area to watch the sun drop into the Andaman Sea.

attractions.name: Wat Chalong
attractions.blurb: Phuket's most revered old temple, where people come to pay respects to Luang Pho Cham. It has a grand chedi and a wide temple ground, and is the island's main merit-making spot.

attractions.name: Phi Phi Islands and island tours
attractions.blurb: Take a boat from Phuket out to the Phi Phi Islands, Maiton Island, and Coral (Hae) Island to snorkel over coral in clear water — a popular day trip for island visitors.

attractions.name: Phang Nga Bay
attractions.blurb: Take a boat out to see the limestone karsts and James Bond Island, and kayak through the caves at Koh Panyee — an easy boat trip to add on from Phuket.
